clue.text: Spin doctor covers every attempt to influence the faithful

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so covers, the second

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the trade of a spin doctor
every means each

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is accused of every trick to sway churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon urging a congregation towards belief and right conduct.

clue.text: Change of direction: Boatman's lost faith

indicators.note: a change of the word direction means its letters are rearranged
lost says the setter's own letter drops out of the word before shuffling

parts.note: the setter Boatman refers to himself, so Boatman's is I (as in I'm, I have)

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that a U-turn in life has cost him his religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boatman's' is 'Boatman has', the setter speaking of himself, so it gives I; 'lost' removes one I from DIRECTION, and 'Change of' rearranges the remaining DRECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a body of teaching held as belief, a faith or creed.

clue.text: Monastic order rejecting impertinent show of levity

indicators.note: order, read as a verb, says the letters of monastic are rearranged
rejecting says the letters for impertinent are thrown out of monastic

parts.note: impertinent means not pertinent, i.e. N/A, not applicable

explanation.surface: Monks expel a cheeky novice for a frivolous display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monastic order' looks like a phrase for a religious community; instead 'order' anagrams MONASTIC once N and A (N/A, 'not applicable' = not pertinent) are rejected, leaving MOSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is light-hearted television entertainment, a programme built for levity.

clue.text: Part from followers of faith over belief, not ignored

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a sect is a body of religious followers

indicators.note: ignored says the word not is dropped from the word for belief

parts.note: a notion is a belief or idea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breakaway group splits from believers over a point of doctrine nobody may ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or division of a whole, the same as a part of it.

clue.text: Chopstick?

parts.note: split the word into chop and stick: the answer means both to split apart and to cling to

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Chopstick' as two words, 'chop' and 'stick': the answer is a verb with those two opposite senses, so this is a double definition disguised as one eating utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave can mean to split with a blow and also to adhere closely, a famous contronym.

clue.text: Salve for concern about family

indicators.note: about says the word for concern goes around the family piece

parts.note: a scare is a worry, a concern
kin means family

explanation.surface: An ointment is offered for worries about relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment, a product used in skin treatment.

clue.text: Chemicals like ratsbane are poisonous, so I tried swallowing ten

indicators.note: swallowing says the scrambled letters take in the ten
poisonous signals the letters of so I tried are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to downing ten doses of deadly arsenic compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisonous' looks like it describes the chemicals but is the anagram signal, making TRIOIDES. Ratsbane is an old name for arsenic trioxide, a rat poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratsbane is arsenic trioxide, so it is an example of an oxide with three oxygen atoms.

clue.text: Boatman's barb: does faith leader come before source of gospel?

indicators.note: come before puts the letter from faith ahead of the evangelist
the leader of faith is its first letter

parts.note: Luke wrote one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: A question about whether the setter's taunt puts belief ahead of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is the barbed blade of an anchor or harpoon, gear a boatman would use.

clue.text: Champ for church service given mark of approval by a small number in report

indicators.note: in report says the pieces are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.words: church service given mark of approval by a small number
parts.note: a Mass is a church service, a tick is a mark of approval and eight is a small number, run together as mass-tick-eight

explanation.surface: A church service is praised by a few in a newspaper account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a winner but is the verb to chew noisily. MASS + TICK + EIGHT, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew vigorously, and to masticate is to chew food.

clue.text: Heartless sinner is no angel?

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its inner part, so heartless strips out the letters spelling inner

parts.note: is no is colloquially ain't, is not

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted wrongdoer is certainly no angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes INNER (a heart is what lies inner) from SINNER, leaving S, followed by AINT. The question mark marks 'angel' as a figurative description.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an angel means they are virtuous and kind, as a holy person is.

clue.text: See 15
Before Man exists … before that? An article of faith

indicators.note: before that puts the article ahead of everything already built
Before puts the word for exists ahead of the letter for man

parts.note: the is the definite article
exists means is
M is the abbreviation for man or male

explanation.surface: A creationist muses on what came before humanity existed.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, a religious faith.

clue.text: Live test match beginning after embarrassment of real unknown getting a duck first

indicators.note: first puts the duck at the very front
after puts the match's opening letter at the end

parts.note: O, a zero score in cricket, is a duck

indicators.note: embarrassment, a disarray, signals the letters of real are jumbled

parts.note: X is the mathematician's unknown quantity

indicators.note: the beginning of match is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket test begins awkwardly as an unknown player is out for nought first ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassment of' rearranges REAL into RALE; in cricket a duck is a score of nought. 'Live' means spoken in person rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral examination is spoken face to face, a live assessment rather than a written paper.

clue.text: End of episcopate? Ask about royal job

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of episcopate
about says the word for ask goes around the royal letter

parts.note: to query is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bishop's departure means asking about a post at court.
explanation.walkthrough: The job is treated as the person who holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the royal household, a post or job.

clue.text: Doubt source of gospel?

parts.note: a question is a doubt, as in there is some question over it
Mark wrote one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: Someone queries where the gospel stories came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's own punctuation: the closing '?' is the mark being described.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol printed at the end of a query is called by this name, punctuation for asking.

clue.text: Act of faith, if led by a woman, gets put down

indicators.note: if led by says the letter for woman would stand at the front, so without it the act remains

parts.note: to write is to put down on paper
W is the abbreviation for woman

explanation.surface: A ceremony performed by a woman is dismissed and disparaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer, led by W, gives WRITE, 'put down'. The surface nods to the row over women leading church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a religious ceremony, a formal act of worship.

clue.text: "Skip eating steak at last" — model

indicators.note: eating says the model takes in the final letter of steak

parts.note: an artist's model is a sitter

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of steak

explanation.surface: A model is told to skip eating steak, quoted as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To skitter is to skip or scamper lightly and quickly.

clue.text: It's eaten or drunk at church in God's first doctrine

parts.note: tea is both a meal eaten and a drink

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of God's

explanation.surface: Bread and wine taken in church are said to embody divine doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA works both ways: an afternoon meal in Britain, and the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaching is a doctrine, a precept handed down by a religion or school of thought.

clue.text: What God may have done for Man, at the heart of faith

definitions.text: What God may have done for Man

indicators.note: the heart of places at in the middle of the word for faith

parts.note: a creed is a faith or set of beliefs

explanation.surface: Creation of humanity sits at the core of belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says God made man, so to have brought him into being is what God did.

clue.text: Contrived to admire Kofi, perhaps

indicators.note: contrived, meaning artificially arranged, signals the letters of to admire are rearranged

explanation.surface: An admirer of Kofi Annan is said to be contrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Kofi Annan, UN Secretary-General, was a noted international peace broker; 'perhaps' shows he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Kofi Annan brokered peace deals, an example of someone acting as go-between in disputes.

clue.text: One article of faith about what Jesus implied?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the article of faith is read backwards

parts.note: a dogma is an article of faith

explanation.surface: A believer reflects on one creed concerning Christ's claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians hold that Jesus claimed divinity, so the declaration is what he implied of himself.

clue.text: Finally, faith in light brown ale is part of this

indicators.note: in places the last letter of faith inside the colour word

parts.note: sandy is a light brown colour

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of faith

explanation.surface: A drinker's belief that pale brown ale belongs in a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy mixes beer, or ale, with lemonade, so ale is one of its components.

clue.text: Ex hypothesi est angelus: the rest you'll get later in the day

definitions.text: the rest you'll get later in the day

indicators.note: Ex says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mock-Latin tag promises an angel will bring the remainder later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex hypothesi' is a Latin phrase meaning by hypothesis; 'Ex' doubles as 'out of', signalling the answer is extracted from the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a rest taken in the early afternoon, the later part of the day.

clue.text: Onset of doubt ends salvation in God — not what was intended

indicators.note: onset of picks the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Doubt creeping in is said to finish salvation, contrary to the divine plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a plan or purpose, the thing someone set out to achieve.

clue.text: Brand of squash

definitions.meaning: a brand is an identifying mark impressed on something
to squash is to crush underfoot

explanation.definitionFit: A stamp is a mark of identity like a brand, and to stamp on something is to crush it flat.

clue.text: Schematic representation of articles of faith

indicators.note: representation of says schematic is presented again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diagram lays out the tenets of a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of religious doctrine set out as questions and answers.

clue.text: Fool has faith leader hold recruits' capital

indicators.note: hold says the leader's name contains the capital letter of recruits'

parts.note: Sun Myung Moon led the Unification Church, the Moonies

indicators.note: capital picks the first letter of recruits'

explanation.surface: A fool lets a cult leader take charge of new members' money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the first letter. Moon founded the Unification Church, known for recruiting followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is a stupid person, an insulting word for a fool.

clue.text: Liberation for limbo-dancing Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner signals the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: limbo dancing is getting under a bar, i.e. getting low
limbo dancing is getting under a bar, i.e. getting low

explanation.surface: Freedom is likened to a dancer bending beneath the limbo bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of GETTING LOW gives the answer, which drops the W in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting go means releasing someone, setting them free, which is liberation.
